newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq attacks Lebanon over Arab games' exclusion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq attacks Lebanon over Arab games' exclusion.

text.p: Iraqi newspapers on Sunday harshly attacked the Lebanese government, with one paper accusing it of making "silly financial profits" out of its refusal of allowing Iraqi athletes to attend the Pan Arab Games opened in Beirut on Saturday.

"Preventing (Iraq's athletic) teams from entering Lebanon in return for silly financial profits means that this goverment has sold its decision with a cheap price," Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel said in a front-page editorial.
Iraqi 97 athletes stranded for two days at the Lebanese border headed home on Saturday after Beirut refused to grant them visas to take part in the games.
Babel, owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, said, "such a decision will not effect Iraq's prestige but it contains (implicit) condemnation of the rulers of Kuwait and Saudi Arabia."
Iraq is blaming the Lebanese decision excluding Iraq from the games on Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
A Lebanese foreign ministry official said on Wednesday Lebanon was under pressure from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia to exclude the Iraqis from the games.

The two countries, Gulf War foes of Iraq and the most generous Arab countries which financed the rebuilding of Beirut sport studium where the games are taking place, threatened to boycott the games if Iraq competed.

Al-Thawra, newspaper of the ruling Baath party, said, "Our expectation has come true...We are living in bad time governed by illgotten finance," in referring to Lebanese refusal to grant visas to Iraqis.
"It is dishonour for us to attend such a sport gathering full of hatred and hostility," the paper added.
The paper also criticised the Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid, saying has done nothing to allow Iraqis attend the games. It accused him of not "sholdering his responsibility."
Meguid intervened on Wednesday in a bid to arrange for a symbolic Iraqi presence at the games.
